description: Nothing sensitive happens without the client's yes: the skill that gives the request a stable shape, the Approvals page it lands on, and the ticket it blocks until an answer comes back
client_copy: Antes de hacer algo que te compromete —mandar un mail, publicar, gastar— te lo pide y espera tu sí.
_comment: IT DEPENDS ON kanban BECAUSE THE SKILL SAYS SO: the request is not a
message, it is a block on the ticket the agent is working. An approval
with no board to sit on is a question nobody ever answers.
THE CORE SURFACE IS THE GATE ITSELF ON THE ENGINE (core/): the row store,
the rendered body and the /portal/approvals routes. On a Hermes agent none
of that is read -- there the gate is the engine's own -- and the folder
just travels with the registry copy.
IT REGISTERS NO TOOLSET. It used to ship two fake sensitive tools so the
gate could be shown to work with nothing real behind it; both are gone now
that the real ones exist (`social`'s publish_instagram, `mail`'s
send_email), each one registered by its own plugin wrapped in
approval_required() and drawing its own card through this one's renderer
hook. What is left here is the whole machinery and none of the verbs.
The gate hook that enforces the rule lives in policy/hooks/gate.py and does
NOT move here: policy/ belongs to the host, mounted read only into the
container, and a plugin never owns policy (notes/plugin-system-plan.md,
